proposed.text: Can an architect transfer copyright in architectural designs to a developer or client through a written assignment agreement?

options.text: No, copyright can never be assigned by an architect
Yes, copyright may be assigned in whole or in part, and inter vivos assignment requires a written indication of that intention
Only if the Board of Architecture approves the transfer in advance
Only after the building has been completed and occupied

rationale.c: The local RA 8293 assignment text does not require Board approval.
rationale.d: Section 180 does not condition assignment on completion or occupancy.
rationale.correct: RA 8293 Section 180.1 allows copyright to be assigned in whole or in part. Section 180.2 states that copyright is not deemed assigned inter vivos unless there is a written indication of that intention. The statute does not require Board approval or building completion for assignment.
rationale.takeaway: Copyright assignment is allowed, but the written-intention requirement matters.
